_comment_about_this_file: Managed-policy template for Google Chrome / Chromium / Brave / Arc.
Drop into one of the platform-specific paths below; values land in
chrome.storage.managed and override anything the user set locally.
macOS:   converted to a .plist and placed at
<EXTENSION_ID>\policy (REG_SZ values), or via GPO using the
provided ADMX/ADML files in this directory.
Replace <EXTENSION_ID> below with the actual 32-char Chrome extension
ID. See docs/enterprise/DEPLOYMENT.md, 'Finding the extension ID'.

_comment_about_runtime_hosts: These two are Chrome's own per-extension host-blocking policy, not
a Sonomos setting. As written here they are a no-op: nothing is
READ THIS IF YOUR FLEET SETS runtime_blocked_hosts FLEET-WIDE. A
default policy that blocks extensions from a broad host pattern
applies to this extension too, and this extension's content scripts
are what screen prompts. Block the AI web surfaces and those scripts
never run: screening stops, the popup still reports a healthy
connection, and prompts go out unexamined. If you run such a policy,
runtime_allowed_hosts for this extension must also name the AI web
surfaces it is injected on (manifest.json content_scripts.matches),
not just the loopback origin the presence beacon uses.

_comment_about_settings: These map 1:1 onto managed-schema.json at the repo root, which is
the authoritative description of every key, its type and its
bounds. Only the names in shared/constants.js::MANAGED_KEYS are
read at all; anything else here is ignored on arrival.
The four keys below are the ones ENFORCED by code that runs today:
allowedProviders  which catalog providers the shim screens
heartbeatSeconds  desktop-app health-probe cadence, 10-600s
debugLogging      healthy-path console lines only; a blocked or
unscreened send is warned about regardless
enforceTimeoutMs  how long a HELD request waits for a verdict
before it is BLOCKED, 1000-120000ms
Two further keys are accepted and then ignored, and are left out
of this template on purpose [documented 2026-09-01]:
`telemetryEnabled` (nothing consults it - the service worker's
handleTelemetry logs unconditionally) and `lockedSettings` (there
is no popup settings UI, so there is nothing for it to lock).
Setting either one changes no behaviour. Both are still declared
in managed-schema.json and still merged into settings, so a policy
that sets them is accepted rather than rejected - which is exactly
why they are named here. See docs/enterprise/DEPLOYMENT.md.
allowedProviders holds CATALOG PROVIDER IDS from
shared/ai-surfaces.json - not product nicknames and not API
endpoint names. The accepted values are the enum in
managed-schema.json (allowedProviders.items.enum); read them
there, because tests/shim.test.js pins that enum against the
catalog and this file is not pinned to anything.
`[]` (below) or an unset key means EVERY catalog surface is
screened. That is the default and the recommended setting. A
non-empty list is SUBTRACTIVE: it can only remove surfaces from
screening, never add one, because the content scripts are declared
against the catalog at build time. What narrowing costs, stated
plainly: a provider left off the list is not screened at all, so
prompts to it leave the machine unexamined. This knob reduces
protection; set it only where somebody has accepted that in
writing. Example - a fleet that holds traffic to two vendors and
has accepted the loss everywhere else:
"allowedProviders": ["openai", "anthropic"]
